title: Sound effects anchored to a word inside a line
description: sfx are placed like turns, after the previous turn ends. Practice: start an effect 100-200 ms before the cue word, or under the line, without covering words. Add an anchor to the next turn, e.g. {sfx phone_ring @next-0.2}, or document the negative-gap pattern if it already covers this.
design:
Write the effect where it happens in the text; the renderer finds the time.

- {sfx phone_ring}                          between lines: plays, the next line waits (today)
- {sfx phone_ring @-0.5}                    between lines, starting 0.5 s before the previous line ends (today)
- vadik: Подключаюсь {sfx modem} к интернету.   inside a line: starts at that word; speech goes on over it
- vadik: {sfx keyboard} Так, пишу.          at the start of a line: under the whole line
- palych: Вон отсюда! {sfx door_close +0.3} after a word, shifted 0.3 s later (negative = earlier)

Mechanics: the marker is stripped from the text sent to TTS (no split turn, so prosody stays whole). The marker position is a character offset into the spoken text. Word timings come from a speech recognizer run on the rendered clip (mlx Whisper with word timestamps, Russian; downloads on first use with the [perform] log line); the effect starts at the start time of the first word after the marker, plus the offset. Fallback when alignment is off or fails: offset = clip length x share of spoken characters before the marker, logged as estimated. timeline.json gets each inline effect with its anchor word and how its time was found (aligned/estimated). The word timings also give timeline.json per-word times (the old README roadmap item). Lint: a cue word in a line («звонит», «стук», «модем», «хлопнула дверь») without an sfx marker in or next to it is a warning, pointing at the word.
acceptance_criteria: An inline marker plays its effect within 0.15 s of the anchor word in a test render (checked against the aligned word time); the line renders as one TTS call; a line with no markers renders byte-identical; docs in scenario and perform skills; episodes 01-03 re-annotated where an effect belongs inside a line.

title: Normalize every rendered episode to -16 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP
description: Apple's podcast spec: -16 LUFS integrated, true peak at or below -1 dBTP (podcasters.apple.com/support/audio-requirements). Today scene.py only scales the mix down when it would clip, so episodes land at whatever level they happen to reach. Add a final loudness step after beds and sfx are mixed (pyloudnorm, already used by calibrate.py), with a --loudness flag (default -16, 0 to skip). Approved by Denis 2026-10-28.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered episode measures -16 +-0.5 LUFS integrated and true peak <= -1 dBTP; timeline.json timings unchanged; one [perform] log line with the measured before/after; --loudness 0 renders as before.
close_reason: master.py + scene.py --loudness; fake render -16.6 LUFS / -1.0 dBTP, --loudness 0 byte-identical, timeline unchanged

title: Fade the bed in and out at episode edges

acceptance_criteria: The last bed fades out over 2-3 s after the final line; the first bed fades in over 1.5 s; heard on episode 3.

title: A/B the ambience bed level: 24 dB vs 18 dB under speech
description: Beds sit 24 dB under speech plus 9 dB ducking. A vendor source puts ambience 12-18 dB under dialogue, so ours may be too quiet to set the scene. Remix episode 2 from its clips at 24, 18 and 15 dB and let Denis pick by ear.
acceptance_criteria: Three remixes sent; Denis's pick becomes ambience.py's default and is written into the perform skill.

title: Check the phone filter against a 300-3400 Hz band-pass

acceptance_criteria: phone_line corners documented in its docstring and within 300-3400 Hz; a phone line in episode 2 sounds like a phone.
